lead: The black-and-white coliseum. The oldest stadium in the elite of Spanish football, with more than a hundred years of history, the second-best stadium in Europe according to The Telegraph and home to one of the most decorated clubs in Spain.

The Camp de Mestalla is not just Valencia CF’s stadium: it is a living monument to the history of Valencia, the oldest stadium in the Spanish top division since 2020 and one of the most emblematic sporting venues in Europe. Pelé, Maradona, Kempes and the best players in football history have run on its pitch. It has survived a civil war, the Great Flood of 1957 and a pandemic. It has hosted the 1982 World Cup, the 1992 Olympic Games and 10 Copa del Rey finals.

Whether or not you are a football fan, the Mestalla Forever Tour is one of the most recommended visits in Valencia: history, emotion and unique architecture in a stadium that has been beating at the heart of the city for more than a century.

items.kicker: The oldest stadium in LaLiga · Opened 1923
items.title: The Stadium · 100 Years of History
items.subtitle: 49,430 spectators · 105 × 68 m · The steepest north stand in Europe
items.body: The Camp de Mestalla is much more than a football stadium: it is the longest-standing coliseum of Spanish elite football. Opened on 20 May 1923 with a friendly between Valencia FC and Levante FC — first goal by Arturo Montesinos, “Montes” — it was born in what were then orchards and farmland next to the irrigation channel that gave it its name. Since January 2020 it has been the oldest stadium in Spain’s top division, following the disappearance of the old San Mamés. The Telegraph ranked it the second-best stadium in Europe, describing its fans as “the most demanding in Spain with the most atmosphere” and its stands as “the steepest compared with any major stadium in Europe”.

items.title: The Mestalla Forever Tour
items.subtitle: Changing rooms · Players’ tunnel · Press room · Walk onto the pitch · Trophy room
items.body: The Mestalla Forever Tour is one of the most popular tourist attractions in Valencia for football lovers — and also for anyone who simply wants to understand why this stadium is a symbol of the city. In about an hour, specialist guides narrate the stadium’s century-old history while you walk through its most emotionally charged corners: the changing rooms where legends such as Kempes, Mendieta or David Villa got dressed; the players’ tunnel that vibrates with the chants of the Gradona; the press room; the fans’ balcony; the VIP box; the chapel; and the walk onto the pitch along the same corridor the players use. It also includes the “Récords Blanquinegres” museum and the official shop.
facts: Changing rooms, tunnel, press room, VIP box, walk onto the pitch, trophy room
Morning visit only · Changing rooms closed · Check at valenciacf.com

items.kicker: One of the most decorated clubs in Spain
items.title: Honours · The Great Titles of Valencia CF
items.subtitle: 6 League titles · 8 Copas del Rey · 1 UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup · 2 European Super Cups
items.body: Valencia CF is one of the greats of Spanish football, with more than a century of history. The 40s were the first golden age: the legendary “electric forward line” of Epi, Amadeo, Mundo, Asensi and Gorostiza won three league titles and two cups. The second golden age came with Kempes in the 80s: Copa del Rey (1979), European Cup Winners’ Cup (1980) and European Super Cup (1980). And the best recent moment, at the turn of the 21st century, with two consecutive league titles (1999–2000 and 2001–02), the Copa del Rey (1999) and two consecutive Champions League finals (2000 and 2001). Mestalla has hosted 10 Copa del Rey finals and 36 matches of the Spanish national team, including the group stage of the 1982 World Cup.
facts: 8 titles · Mestalla has hosted 10 Copa del Rey finals
1 UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup (1980) · 2 European Super Cups (1980, 2004) · 13 Champions
Kempes, Maradona, Pelé · They have played on this pitch

items.kicker: The essence of Mestalla · The most electric atmosphere in Spain
items.title: La Gradona · The Steepest North Stand
items.subtitle: Extreme slope · Unique atmosphere in Europe · Home fans’ end
items.body: La Gradona — as the north end of Mestalla is popularly known — is the reason this stadium has a unique personality in European football. Its vertical stands, with a slope that makes your hair stand on end even for those who have seen them a thousand times, create an unrivalled acoustic that turns every match into an exceptional auditory experience. It is the end where Valencia CF’s most active fans gather, the ones who sing for all 90 minutes, the ones who create that atmosphere The Telegraph described as the most intense in Spain. Attending a match with the Gradona full is one of the most authentic football experiences on the continent.
facts: The greatest of any major stadium in Europe · Unique in Spain
The most intense atmosphere in LaLiga · Described by The Telegraph as unique

items.kicker: A living monument of the city · Beyond football
items.title: Mestalla in the History of Valencia
items.subtitle: 1982 World Cup · Barcelona 1992 Olympics · Copa del Rey · 2025 Nations League
items.body: Mestalla is a venue that goes beyond Valencia CF football. It has hosted three groups of the group stage of the Spain 1982 World Cup, Olympic matches at the Barcelona 1992 Games, 10 Copa del Rey finals and 36 matches of the Spanish national team. In 2025 it hosted the second leg of the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals. Pelé, Maradona, Kempes, Maldini, Ronaldo and the best players in history have run on its pitch. During the Civil War it served as a concentration camp and scrap-metal store; it survived the Great Flood of 1957; and during the 2020 pandemic it was a distribution centre for the Food Bank. A stadium with a memory.
facts: 3 group-stage matches · Spain’s World Cup debut
Football venue of the Barcelona Olympic Games (except the final)
2025 · Quarter-finals · Mestalla as the home of the Spanish national team

items.kicker: New stadium under construction · Av. de les Corts Valencianes
items.title: Nou Mestalla · The Club’s Future
items.subtitle: Planned for ~70,000 seats · The future of Valencia CF in Valencia
items.body: The Nou Mestalla is the stadium of the future of Valencia CF, planned on the Avenida de les Corts Valencianes, in the Benicalap district. Works began in 2007 and were halted for years by financial problems and the crisis, and have now resumed. The new stadium is planned to have around 70,000 seats and to become one of the most modern venues in Europe. In the meantime, the Camp de Mestalla remains the club’s home and the stage of Valencia CF’s living history. The coexistence of the century-old stadium that waits and the future under construction is part of the club’s current identity.

~70,000 seats · One of the largest in Spain

blocks.title: Tips for visiting Mestalla
items: The Mestalla Forever Tour does not require advance booking — but buy your ticket online at valenciacf.com to avoid waiting
If you happen to be there for a LaLiga match, the atmosphere of the north Gradona is a priceless experience
On match days the tour only runs in the morning and the changing room is closed — check the calendar beforehand
The official shop is on the tour route: perfect for taking home the most Valencianista souvenir
The stadium is 15 min on foot from the centre and 5 min from the metro (L5 Aragón stop) — no need for a car
For the Paris 2024 Olympic Games and major national-team events, Mestalla remains a regular venue — check the calendar
